bugs.what: 'oil the mechanism' action was available and consumed a turn/HP even though I hadn't used the oil flask on it yet — the flask sat unused in inventory with no visible effect on success odds; the action seems to be a flat STR check independent of having the right item, which undercuts the point of collecting the oil flask.

confusions: No inventory-view action exists, so I couldn't confirm whether the oil flask, tinderbox, cutlass, or iron key were actually being used by contextual actions — items seem to vanish into an invisible inventory with no way to check their state.

No healing/rest mechanic anywhere (tavern, cottage) despite combat and repeated STR-check failures draining HP steadily; at hp3/10 I had no recovery option and had to gamble on a ~55% mechanism check.

'oil the mechanism' failure message ('the wrench slips') implies a specific tool (wrench) that was never given to or mentioned to the player, making the fail state feel arbitrary rather than skill-based.
suggestions: Add a way to inspect current inventory/items without spending a turn.
Show item requirements or success-odds hints before risky HP-costing actions (combat, STR checks) so players can decide whether to retreat and prepare.
Add at least one low-cost healing/rest option, since repeated skill-check failures can chain into death with no recovery path.
Make the oil flask visibly required/consumed by the 'oil the mechanism' action so collecting it feels causally connected to success.
